SB 213/FA 213/AP
Senate Bill 213 By: Senators Kirkpatrick of the 32nd, Cowsert of the 46th, Albers of the 56th, Rhett of the 33rd, Summers of the 13th and others
AS PASSED SENATE
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Part 2 of Article 15 of Chapter 1 of Title 10 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the "Fair Business Practices Act of 1975," so as … end of paragraph (34), by replacing the period with "; and" at the end of paragraph (35), and by adding a new paragraph to read as follows: "(36) Failure to comply with the provisions of Code Section 10-1-393.20."
SB 213/FA 213/AP
SECTION 2. Said part is further amended by adding a new Code section to read as follows: "10-1-393.20. (a) As used in this Code section, the term: (1) 'Assessment task' means any assignment, essay, thesis, dissertation, report, examination, project, … firm, limited liability company, association, corporation, or other legal entity or unincorporated organization. (7) 'Private school' shall have the same meaning as private school set forth in subsection (b) of Code Section 20-2-690. (8) 'Student or examinee' means:
SB 213/FA 213/AP
(A) Any student of a local school system or public school, a private school, or a home study program in this state; (B) Any student of an institution of the University System of Georgia or a unit of the … or (2) Prohibit any person from providing an automated system, software, or platform that generates specific responses to a student's or examinee's prompts; provided, however, that such responses shall not constitute a substantially completed assessment task and the
SB 213/FA 213/AP
primary purpose of such automated system, software, or platform is not the provision of assessment tasks."
SECTION 3. Said part is further amended in subsection (a) of Code Section 10-1-399, relating to civil actions for violations and remedies, by striking "Any" at the beginning of subsection (a), and inserting "Except as otherwise provided, any" in lieu thereof.
SECTION 4. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
